To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the mixture model with a single component is a better model for document scores than the mixture model with two components, (ii) the mixture model is a better model than a single distribution model, and (iii) the mixture model does not perform as well as a single distribution model in terms of predicting the number of documents relevant to a query.

the distribution of document score values returned in response to a given query can be modelled as a mixture distribution, that the parameters of the mixture distribution can be estimated using a maximum likelihood method, and that these parameters can be used to infer the relevance of unseen documents.

the mixture distribution of document scores is a mixture of a Gaussian and a point mass, with the point mass at the maximum document score, and that the mixture distribution can be used to predict the number of relevant documents in the top 1000 documents retrieved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
1. The development of a new document scoring distribution model, which is based on an extension of the beta-binomial distribution.
the development of a new hypothesis, the Gaussian Mixture Hypothesis (GMH) which is based on a Gaussian mixture model.

(1) the modelling of document scores returned by IR systems using parametric distributions; (2) the use of such models to predict the distribution of scores for new queries; (3) the use of the score distribution model for the prediction of document relevance; and (4) the use of score distributions to evaluate the effectiveness of IR systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single model that fits all queries.
the document scores distribution is a mixture of a number of distributions and the number and type of these distributions are query-dependent.
there is a need for further research to be carried out in order to determine the best model for document scores.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mixture distribution of document scores can be modelled by a mixture of exponential families, with a mixture of Gaussian distributions being a special case.
we have found that the most successful of these hypotheses are those that are based on the notion that the scores returned from a system are drawn from a mixture of a number of distributions.

, for the majority of the datasets we have examined, the best performing model is a mixture of two normal distributions with a common variance and a mixture of three normal distributions with a shared variance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of document score is a mixture of two or more component distributions.
the score distribution of an IR system is a function of the query.
the mixture of two Gaussian (M2G) model is not a suitable model for document scores.
